title.narrative: Integrated Conservation Management and Restoration of High-Value Landscapes in Uzbekistan

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
To scale innovative integrated approaches to ecosystem restoration and conservation to catalyze transformational shifts in three high value landscapes in Uzbekistan.

YesDetails on the project’s socio-economic benefits are discussed in the relevant section of the Prodoc (p. 26). The project will have direct beneficiaries through multiple project outputs, and there are multiple pathways for direct engagement of stakeholders at the local level who will benefit. One key activity where the project will work directly with local beneficiaries is in the establishment of at least 4 Pasture User Associations, under Output 2.1. The establishment of PUAs will involve multiple villages, with thousands of inhabitants. This is where the project will generate benefits for the largest number of people, and it is conservatively estimated that the project will benefit approximately 28,000 people (14,000 women, 14,000 men), depending on the final selection of villages that confirm their participation once the project starts. The improved sustainability of pasture management resulting from the establishment of the PUAs will mean that each family dependent on livestock for their livelihoods will be able to generate greater and more secure income over the long-term, and also will have increased resilience to climate impacts. Also under Output 2.1, the forest management unit staff from the participating leskhozes will have their capacities improved, covering a total of approximately 500 people (50 women, 450 men; this imbalance between men and women is based on the existing gender distribution among forest agency employees; the project will try to improve this situation). Under Output 2.3 the project design includes a specific opportunity to support sustainable livelihoods in communities participating in the sustainable pasture management activities, making targeted investments to further reduce pressure on natural resources through support for alternative fuel and more efficient household stoves, value-added processing, and livestock facilities. Under Output 2.4, the staff of the existing protected areas will also be trained and better equipped; current data indicates there are 100 staff (20 women, 80 men) for the two PAs that will receive the majority of project support, Nuratau State Nature Reserve (49 staff) and Surkhan State Nature Reserve (51 staff).
